title: When writing a long cookie name and value to a Netscape cookie jar, a remote HTTP server can make curl write a record that exceeds its line-length… (CVE-2026-92386)
description: A vulnerability in curl causes it to write cookie records exceeding line-length limits when a remote HTTP server sets long cookie names and values in a Netscape cookie jar. This results in subsequent curl invocations silently aborting cookie parsing upon encountering the overly long line, ignoring valid cookies that follow.
aiSummary: When curl writes a long cookie name and value to a Netscape cookie jar, a remote HTTP server can cause curl to write a record that exceeds the line-length parsing limit. This malformed cookie record causes any subsequent curl command reading from the same cookie jar with the --cookie option to silently stop parsing at the long line, ignoring all valid cookies after it. This behavior can disrupt cookie handling in curl but does not include details on further exploitation or impact beyond cookie parsing interruption.
aiImpact: The vulnerability causes curl to silently abort parsing of cookie files when encountering an excessively long cookie record, leading to ignored valid cookies that follow. This can disrupt applications relying on curl's cookie handling, potentially affecting session management or authentication flows that depend on those cookies. There is no information about remote code execution or other severe impacts.
